questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to result in a high quality product?
options: Using appropriate production processes
Assessing available Government rebates
Developing good functional and/or aesthetic features
Implementing environmentally friendly production processes
questions.explanation: Quality is judged by how well a product performs its function and how appealing it is, so good functional and/or aesthetic features are the strongest contributor. The other options relate to production, finance or environmental factors rather than the inherent quality of the design.

questions.q: Which of the following contributes most to sustainability during manufacturing?
options: Analysing the economic aspects
Monitoring the amount of energy used
Recycling materials to minimise waste
Using materials and processes that have minimal effect on the environment
questions.explanation: Sustainable manufacturing is best achieved by selecting materials and processes that have minimal impact on the environment across the whole product life cycle. Recycling and monitoring energy are useful measures, but choosing low-impact materials and processes addresses sustainability most directly.

questions.q:
The final prototype of a new product was evaluated and its features and functions were closely examined.

What was being determined by this evaluation?
options: Whether it is aesthetically pleasing
Whether it performs its desired functions
Whether it is a quality solution to the design problem
Whether it will sell the greatest number of units at the best price
questions.explanation: Evaluating a final prototype against its features and functions tests how well it solves the original design problem overall. Aesthetics and function are individual criteria within that judgement, while sales potential is a market outcome rather than what the prototype evaluation determines.

questions.q: Which of the following strategies is most likely to influence the use of energy saving devices by consumers?
options: Adhering to industrial patents
Integrating emerging technology
Releasing the product at a suitable time
Evaluating current marketing techniques
questions.explanation: Timing a product's release to suit consumer readiness and market conditions most strongly influences whether energy saving devices are taken up. Patents, technology and marketing analysis support development, but a well-timed release drives consumer adoption.

questions.q:
The users of current social networking applications on a computer and/or mobile phone, grouped by age, are shown in the stimulus graphs.

Computer users by age — 10–19: 16%, 20–29: 17%, 30–39: 18%, 40–49: 25%, 50–59: 18%, 60–69: 6%.
Mobile phone users by age — 10–19: 14%, 20–29: 20%, 30–39: 21%, 40–49: 23%, 50–59: 13%, 60–69: 9%.

Which age group would be best to target for research into the development of a new social networking application?
options: 50–59 year olds
40–49 year olds
30–39 year olds
20–29 year olds
questions.explanation: Interpreting the data, the 40–49 age group shows the highest combined use across both computer (25%) and mobile phone (23%), making it the largest existing user base to research. Targeting the group with the greatest current usage gives the most reliable data for development.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the nature of entrepreneurial activity?
options: It provides financial backing and technical support for a new product.
It provides inspiration and creativity in the development of a new product.
It takes responsibility for the creative and social aspects of a new product.
It assumes the responsibility, vision and economic support for a new product.
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur takes on the responsibility, vision and economic risk of bringing a new product to market. The other options describe only a single aspect — finance, creativity or social responsibility — rather than the full entrepreneurial role.

questions.q: At which point in the design process would a working prototype be most useful to communicate design solutions?
options: When setting up for production
When analysing problems with production
When developing initial concepts with designers
When presenting the final design to the focus group
questions.explanation: A working prototype best communicates the finished design solution when presented to a focus group, who can experience and respond to a realistic model. Early concept work uses sketches and models, while production stages rely on technical documentation rather than communicating the solution.

questions.q: A design team works best when
options: tasks are allocated to individuals based on expertise.
the designer’s work flow is structured and organised.
design teams work in direct competition with each other.
team members always work independently towards a goal.
questions.explanation: Effective collaborative design teams allocate tasks according to each member's expertise so the right skills are applied to each part of the project. Constant competition or working independently undermines the cooperation that makes a team productive.

questions.q: What is the most likely reason for designers and manufacturers to use environmentally friendly resources?
options: To maintain resources for future use
To increase environmental awareness
To ensure the use of recycled materials
To improve the quality of the natural environment
questions.explanation: Using environmentally friendly resources reflects sustainability — conserving resources so they remain available for future generations. The other options are secondary benefits rather than the primary reason for choosing such resources.

questions.q: What are the primary considerations when designing products to meet the needs of society?
options: Individual needs and wants
Social trends and expectations
Cultural expectations and beliefs
Environmental implications and expectations
questions.explanation: Designing for the needs of society means responding to broad social trends and expectations that affect the whole community. Individual, cultural and environmental factors are relevant, but social trends are the primary consideration when designing for society as a whole.

There is growing consumer demand for innovative products that enhance the quality of life.

Explain a range of factors that contribute to the success of these products.

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident between a range of factors and the contribution to the success of innovations and enhancement of life quality
Provides characteristics and features of factors that contribute to the success of innovations and demonstrates a link to enhance quality of life
Sketches in general terms a factor that contributes to the success of innovations OR indicates the features of successful innovations

questions.topic: Factors affecting design and design practices
questions.q:
Many products are designed to have a limited ‘lifespan’ – that is, they are designed to be replaced rather than repaired.

Give reasons why designers develop new products with a limited ‘lifespan’.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines reasons why designers develop new products with a limited lifespan
Identifies a reason why designers develop new products

questions.topic: Societal trends impact on society and environment
questions.q:
Many products are designed to have a limited ‘lifespan’ – that is, they are designed to be replaced rather than repaired.

Explain the effects on society and the environment of designing products with a limited lifespan.

criteria.descriptor: Makes evident the relationship between the limited lifespan of a product and the effects on both society and the environment
Provides characteristics and features of the effects on society and/or the environment as a result of a product’s limited lifespan
Sketches in general terms an effect on society and/or the environment as a result of a product’s limited lifespan
Identifies a societal or environmental effect

questions.q: What activities would a designer undertake to determine whether an existing product needs further development?

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident between how designers further develop existing products AND the need for the redesigned product
Provides characteristics and features of activities undertaken by designers when determining a need to redesign an existing product
Sketches in general terms activities undertaken by designers with a link to the redesign of an existing product
Identifies an activity undertaken by designers in redesigning an existing product OR identifies a need for further developing an existing design

questions.q: Analyse why it may be necessary to further develop an existing product even though the current model is still functional and aesthetically appealing.

criteria.descriptor: Draws out and relates implications of reasons for further developing an existing product with reference to function and aesthetics
Provides reasons why and/or how designers further develop an existing product with reference to function and aesthetics
Identifies issues and provides evidence relating to why designers further develop an existing product
Provides characteristics and features relating to why designers further develop existing product
Sketches in general terms a reason why designers further develop an existing product
Identifies a reason for further developing an existing product
